feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization support seniority and trustworthiness.  
- Strong scope and relevance: web, email, social, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and governance are all well covered for a digital strategy lead profile.  
- Good use of scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add weight.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes, not just responsibilities: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, process efficiency, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to make the CV tighter and easier to scan.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “workflows and systems”); standardize bullet formatting since some roles use paragraph-plus-dashes rather than clean bullets.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a clearer leadership/value proposition would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your seniority and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter phrase like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel programs across web, email, social, content, and multimedia. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and building the workflows, governance, and systems that help mission-driven organizations communicate at scale. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, cross-functional stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communication.”
- “Workflows and systems” is repeated across the intro, Core Competencies, and multiple experience bullets.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and pluralize for consistency: “Multi-channel communications,” “Editorial workflows,” “Stakeholder coordination.”
- Prioritize strategic/leadership strengths over task-level items; e.g. replace “Web & CMS administration” with “Web platform strategy & CMS governance.”
- Make systems language more specific and less repetitive: combine “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Web platform strategy & CMS governance • Multi-channel communications • Editorial workflows & content operations • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already covered in the header and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented experience entry. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 2–3 highest-impact contributions, especially platform modernization and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 concise impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, publishing speed, search/discovery improvements.
- Example rewrite: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with the “Recent Projects” section; avoid repeating the same microsite and AI search details verbatim in both places.
- “Governance, workflows, and analytics” also echoes the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new here (consulting scope, current delivery, AI/search, hands-on build work).

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email list size, engagement, growth, campaign performance, or follower growth if available; otherwise shorten to avoid a vague “tens of thousands/thousands.”
- Strengthen results language in later bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast-quality studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting stack to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Video/programming leadership overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on scaling/building infrastructure, not recurring production.
- Editorial coordination/governance also appears earlier; emphasize enterprise systems and modernization here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, operational ownership, and channel growth distinct from the later director role and earlier producer role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with ownership + scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving coordination of editorial and advocacy messaging.”
- Combine newsletter and workflow points into one stronger bullet with scale: “Oversaw production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders, improving publishing consistency and cross-team coordination.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace “helped” phrasing with direct action verbs: strengthened, streamlined, standardized, coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier Digital Media Manager / Producer role; clarify this role as scaling/operationalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than repeating generic communications phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “content planning” for a more senior phrase like “content operations” or “audience strategy” to better match director/consultant-level work.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web and content strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Keep terminology aligned with recent roles: “governance,” “operations,” and “enterprise” are stronger than “messaging.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo bullets; “communications” is broader and less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or older tools unless they are job-target critical; consider removing jQuery first.
- Group SharePoint/Power Pages as “enterprise content platforms” if both are not central to recent work.
- If space allows, tie to scale/impact indirectly: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web properties,” consistent with recent Drupal work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating it verbatim in multiple places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT, so this section should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools after the strategic skills: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten wording and order by impact: strategy/reporting first, tools second, optimization last
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive reporting • SEO & performance analysis • GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use Topline Skills for higher-level strengths, not another software inventory.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better phrased as “executive reporting” for clarity and stronger senior-level positioning.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and distinctive from the broader multimedia references elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Studio, Livestream & Hybrid Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Hybrid/virtual event production • Run-of-show and technical coordination**
- If space allows, emphasize leadership/ownership over task execution: use **studio systems** and **technical coordination** instead of just **editing**.
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add scale language such as **multi-camera**, **broadcast-quality**, or **high-stakes live event delivery**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is broad and repeats experience already shown in multiple NACo roles.
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies; differentiate this item by focusing on studio/event delivery and technical operations.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Use this space to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat generic names.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want this section to stay purely technical, remove weaker/less central items unless you’ve used them materially in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats the **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry; differentiate by adding proficiency/context here or trimming one version.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and the most current, differentiating tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling by use case: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “supporting Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and lightweight automation for high-traffic public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you specifically want this section to reflect implementation tooling.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and group by function.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a flat list to a capability-led line: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first: keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; consider dropping one or two lower-value/general tools.
- If accurate, add scope in a parenthetical for impact: “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals, campaign coordination, and reporting workflows.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack and Teams are very common and may add little unless space allows.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the roles described, but this item is too bare and misses the scale/ownership implied elsewhere in the CV. It would be stronger if framed around enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than just listing vendor names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these were hands-on systems you actively administered or used for campaign execution.
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Enterprise email and member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first; order by recency/relevance, not alphabetically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about newsletters/email; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- Avoid adding “analytics,” “automation,” or “campaign strategy” here since those are already covered elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” scope, and team-building contributions without repeating website/video points covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around concrete delivery: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Replace “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with specifics if available: number of livestreams, cadence/audience of video updates, size of team supported, or process improvements introduced.
- Consider ending with leadership scope: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate,” or, if stronger, “supervised/trained…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version framed as launching/building the capability, not scaling it.
- “Website refresh” may feel repetitive with the later Drupal redesign; position this as an earlier refresh, not a major modernization.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts” to distinguish it from later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research projects supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Condense the remaining media work into one sharper clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience growth, participating departments, or types/volume of research projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on research/program support plus the podcast first.
- Avoid broad “supported organizational programs and policy work” phrasing unless you can specify project type or stakeholder impact.
